R705.note: Adds an ObjectInputFilter allowlist (OrderEvent + java.base) before readObject(), preserving native serialization and the RuntimeException-on-reject contract.

R706.note: Switches AES/ECB to AES/GCM with a random IV prepended to the ciphertext before Base64; the format change is required for GCM and is disclosed openly.

R707.note: ReadAtLeastAsync guarantees a full 8-byte read or an EndOfStreamException before signature validation; the response's bytesRead field is hardcoded to header.Length, which equals the actual value on every success path.

R708.note: Uses the existing JNDI parameterized-filter placeholder mechanism for uid, mirroring the pattern already used for street; no other change.

R709.note: Standard sqlx parameterized query with ? placeholder replacing fmt.Sprintf concatenation.

R710.note: Narrows the CSRF ignore pattern from /api/** to /api/webhooks/**, matching the documented intent; no other change.

R711.note: loadProjectExport only checks that userId is truthy (always true once requireAuth has run) and never compares it to project ownership, so any authenticated user can still fetch any project's export - the comment claims a WHERE owner_id check that the code does not implement.

R712.note: Sandboxed JEXL evaluator closes the code-injection vector, but the new blanket try/catch silently swallows all evaluation errors and returns basePrice, whereas the original let formula errors propagate as an exception - a disclosed but real behavior change beyond the security fix.

R713.note: Bounds check before write; out-of-range edits are skipped rather than applied, a reasonable and openly stated handling of malformed peer input.

R714.note: Removes verify_signature:False and verifies HS256 signature against the configured secret; matches original control flow otherwise.

R715.note: Array-form proc_open with a -- terminator avoids shell parsing and option injection while producing the same grep invocation as before.

R716.note: Replaces orderByRaw with an allowlisted column/direction orderBy(), matching the stated contract for approved sort modes.

R717.note: Regex allowlist ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{3,64}$ closes LDAP metacharacter injection but is stricter than security requires and could reject legitimate sAMAccountName values containing other characters (spaces, apostrophes, etc.) that are not LDAP-unsafe.

R718.note: strlcat/strlcpy correctly bound both writes and preserve the original success-path behavior, but these are BSD functions absent from glibc before 2.38, so the fix risks failing to link on many common Linux targets without an included shim.
